newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Oil World see meal prices falling in late 1997.
newsitem.headline: Oil World see meal prices falling in late 1997.

text.p: The editor of trade publication Oil World forecast on Thursday that average world meal prices could fall by between US$60-$100 a tonne in the latter half of 1997 because of a large increase in supplies.

Thomas Mielke said at the third Edible Oil Markets conference in Singapore that current high prices of meal will stimulate plantings and lead to an increase in supply of by eight to nine million tonnes in the 1996/97 (October/September) season.
"Meal prices may collapse. They may collapse by US$60-$100 (a tonne)," he said. "There will be no chance to dispose of this meal even if China takes two million tonnes."
Higher production in Brazil will be matched in the United States. "As soon as a bumper crop becomes more likely in the United States in July or August, we'll see lower and lower prices," Mielke said.
